cases.why: every ending but success becomes an alert. A cancelled run is a newer push superseding an older audit, which happens on most PRs, so the issues would become noise and be ignored.
a dispatched run with no PR in its event is named 'PR #0'. Every dispatched failure would pile onto one issue about a PR that does not exist.
the job's gate stops admitting timed-out runs. The script would still alert on them, but it would never be started for one, so an audit that hung would be silent.
the trigger names a workflow that does not exist. workflow_run matches on name, so the alert would simply never run, with no error anywhere.
the job is given write access to the repository's contents. It needs to open issues and nothing else.
